title: Next.js Data Fetching & Caching: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before notes on fetching in server components, static vs dynamic rendering, revalidation, the Next.js caches, Suspense streaming and generateStaticParams. Ordered from mental model to production mistakes, ending with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Data Fetching Mental Model
points: Server components are async: `const res = await fetch(url)` runs on the server and ships only rendered output, with no client JS for the fetch
Fetch where the data is used; the same URL requested in several components is deduplicated within one render pass
Direct DB or ORM calls work in server components with no API route, but they are not auto-deduplicated; wrap them in React `cache()`
Server-only secrets and tokens stay safe in server components; never pass them as props to client components
Independent requests: start them together with `Promise.all`, because sequential awaits create a waterfall

chapters.title: Static vs Dynamic Rendering
points: Static rendering: HTML is built at build time (or on revalidate) and served from cache; dynamic rendering builds per request
A route becomes dynamic when it uses request-time APIs: `cookies()`, `headers()`, `searchParams`, or an uncached fetch under the version's caching defaults
Comparison: static = fastest and CDN-cacheable but can go stale; dynamic = always fresh but costs server time per request
Force a mode with route segment config `export const dynamic = 'force-static' | 'force-dynamic'`
Check the build output: ○ means static, ƒ means dynamic; one request-time API in a layout makes every child route dynamic

chapters.title: Revalidation: Time-Based and On-Demand
points: Time-based: `fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 60 } })` or `export const revalidate = 60` serves cached data, then refreshes in the background after 60s (stale-while-revalidate)
On-demand by path: `revalidatePath('/blog')` in a server action or route handler invalidates that route's cache
On-demand by tag: tag with `fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })`, then call `revalidateTag('posts')` to refresh every fetch carrying that tag
Comparison: time-based is simple but can serve stale data until the timer fires; on-demand is exact but needs a trigger such as a mutation or webhook
With several revalidate values on one route, the lowest value wins for the page; call revalidation after the mutation, not before

chapters.title: The Next.js Caches
points: Request Memoization: dedupes identical fetch calls during a single server render; lives for one request only
Data Cache: persists fetch results across requests and deployments on the server; controlled by `revalidate`, tags and `cache: 'force-cache' | 'no-store'`
Full Route Cache: stores the rendered HTML and RSC payload of static routes at build time; invalidated when the Data Cache is revalidated or on redeploy
Router Cache: client-side in-memory cache of visited route segments, so back and forward navigation is instant; `router.refresh()` clears it

Comparison by scope: Memoization = one request, Data Cache = server across requests, Full Route Cache = server per route, Router Cache = browser per session; check your version's docs, because the defaults for fetch caching and the Router Cache have changed between releases

chapters.title: Streaming, Suspense and generateStaticParams
points: Streaming sends HTML in chunks so the shell shows first and slow parts fill in later, which improves time to first byte and perceived speed
Wrap a slow async server component in `<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>`; only that subtree waits, and the rest of the page renders at once
`loading.tsx` in a route folder is an automatic Suspense boundary around the page, giving an instant loading state on navigation
`generateStaticParams` returns an array like `[{ slug: 'a' }, { slug: 'b' }]` so dynamic routes such as `/blog/[slug]` are pre-rendered at build time
Unlisted params render on demand by default, and `dynamicParams = false` returns 404 for them; you can also pre-render only the top pages and let the rest generate on first visit

chapters.title: Common Mistakes and Cheat Sheet
points: Mistake: fetching in a client component via useEffect when a server component would do; this adds a waterfall and ships extra JS
Mistake: awaiting requests one after another instead of `Promise.all`
Mistake: using `cookies()` or `headers()` high in the tree and silently making the whole route dynamic
Mistake: revalidating before the mutation finishes, or forgetting to tag fetches that `revalidateTag` should hit

Cheat sheet: `revalidate = N` timed | `revalidatePath` / `revalidateTag` on demand | `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` per-request | `<Suspense>` streams | `generateStaticParams` pre-renders | `router.refresh()` clears the Router Cache
